subject: Post-demo: prompt/output residency, logging, and retention confirmation
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica King <jessica.king@medorahealth.com>, compliance@medorahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T15:12:00-04:00
Subject: Post-demo: prompt/output residency, logging, and retention confirmation

Hi Jessica / Medora compliance team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — really appreciated the thoughtful questions on data handling. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the specifics we discussed and confirm the items you asked us to commit to for the POC. High-level asks I noted from your side:
- Confirm exactly what prompt text and generated outputs Redwood persists by default (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Residency requirements (us-only / specific region preference).
- Retention windows (TTL) for prompt payloads, outputs, and audit logs; ability to reduce/disable retention.
- Logging granularity: request/response payloads vs metadata-only logs; ability to mask or redact fields.
- Evidence: SOC 2 artifact and a short retention matrix for procurement.

Quick summary of what was demoed and our proposed defaults (we'll follow up with written commitments):
- Hosted API (default): prompt payloads and outputs are accessible to Redwood by default and retained for 30 days for debugging/quality improvements.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): customer data isolation; retention is configurable by the customer; Redwood can operate with "ephemeral outputs" for POCs where outputs are not persisted.
- Private / on-prem: customer-managed storage; Redwood does not persist anything unless configured.
- Audit logs: by default we retain control-plane audit logs 365 days for enterprise plans; application-level request traces can be reduced to 90/30 days on request.
- KV cache / streaming buffers: ephemeral in-memory only and not written to disk unless explicitly enabled.

Questions for you (so we can finalize the POC configuration):
1) Will Medora send PHI/PII in prompts for the POC? If yes, please list the classes (e.g., patient names, MRNs).
2) Residency: confirm "us-east-1" is acceptable or specify a region.
3) Retention target: do you require zero-persistence for outputs (ephemeral mode) or a short TTL (e.g., 7 days)?

I'll loop legal and our compliance engineer (Ben) so we can produce the retention matrix and SOC2 excerpt you requested. Attached I'll add a one-page retention matrix and the SOC2 summary after internal alignment. Next step: if you confirm PHI and residency, we'll flip on ephemeral config on your demo key and send updated DPA language for procurement.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: Jessica King <jessica.king@medorahealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@medorahealth.com, procurement@medorahealth.com
Date: 2028-06-05T16:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt/output residency, logging, and retention confirmation

Thanks, Sofia — great demo. A few clarifications from our side so we can decide on POC scope: 

- Medora will send PHI in prompts for the POC (patient names, MRNs, limited notes). We need to make sure outputs are not persisted in a way that can be reconstructed later.
- Residency: prefer us-east-1 only.
- Retention: for POC we'd like outputs to be non-persistent (ephemeral). For logging we can accept a short TTL but need to understand what exactly you keep for debugging (full payloads vs metadata).

Can you confirm whether the "30 day hosted retention" you mentioned is configurable at account level or if it's baked into hosted? Also need a brief description of what you store in audit logs vs request logs.

If you can send a one-page matrix and SOC2 summary, procurement will move quickly.

Best,
Jessica
Jessica King
Head of Product, Medora Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jessica King <jessica.king@medorahealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T09:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt/output residency, logging, and retention confirmation

Hi all — following up with specifics so Medora's compliance and procurement teams have a clear starting point. I'm including the concise answers here; I'll attach the retention matrix and SOC2 summary to the thread.

Clarifications / commitments:
1) Hosted API (standard): default behavior is 30-day retention of prompts and outputs for debugging/quality. However, for accounts under an active sales POC we can enable an "ephemeral mode" that prevents persistence of outputs and drops prompt text after tokenization/anonymization. Ephemeral mode is an account-level toggle we can apply before POC keys are issued.

2) Dedicated (redwood-managed dedicated capacity): data is logically isolated to your pool. Retention is configurable; by default we do not enforce additional retention unless requested. We can commit to disabling persisted outputs for Medora's dedicated pool.

3) Private / on-prem: nothing leaves your environment unless you configure export or managed ingestion — effectively zero-persistence by default.

4) Audit and operational logs: control-plane audit logs (who changed config, model rollouts, key events) are retained 365 days and are available for export. Request-level telemetry (request timestamps, latency, token counts) are retained 90 days by default but can be shortened to 30 or 7 on request. Full request/response payloads are only retained if persistence is enabled; otherwise only metadata is kept for rate-limiting and debugging.

5) Token-level masking and redaction: we support field-level redaction on the client side (recommended) and server-side masking for known PHI fields. We recommend using client-side hashing for explicit patient identifiers for additional protection.

Attachments in this message: redwood-data-retention-matrix.pdf (one-page matrix with hosted/dedicated/private/TL; includes TTLs and regional notes), soc2-type2-summary.pdf (redacted excerpt).

If Medora confirms PHI for the POC we will:
- Enable ephemeral outputs on the demo account.
- Restrict region to us-east-1.
- Set request payload retention to 0 days for stored outputs and 7 days anonymized metadata for rate-limiting only.

@Jessica — once you confirm, Sofia and I will draft the DPA appendix language and push a HubSpot note with the commitments.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica King <jessica.king@medorahealth.com>, compliance@medorahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@medorahealth.com
Date: 2028-06-08T10:23:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt/output residency, logging, and retention confirmation

Jessica / Medora team — thanks for confirming. Per Ben's notes, and to make the POC operational today, here are the commitments Redwood will apply to Medora's demo account (we'll include these in the DPA appendix):

Committed POC configuration (effective immediately for demo keys):
- Ephemeral outputs enabled: generated outputs will not be written to persistent storage.
- Prompt payload handling: prompts will be tokenized and anonymized server-side; full-text prompt persistence = 0 days.
- Residency: compute and any short-lived buffers restricted to us-east-1.
- Request telemetry: anonymized metadata for rate-limiting retained 7 days; full payloads not retained.
- Audit logs: control-plane audit logs retained 365 days (system changes only), available as export for compliance review.

Attachments sent: redwood-data-retention-matrix.pdf, soc2-type2-summary.pdf, medora-ephemeral-config.json (example config we will apply to your demo key).

Next steps / asks for Medora:
1) Confirm you accept the POC commitments above (reply-all).
2) Send the list of PHI fields you expect to include in prompts (we recommended hashing MRNs but will accept if you prefer).
3) Procurement: confirm DPA counterparty name and signatory and we'll push the DPA appendix draft to the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/RWD-1293

I'll mark this in HubSpot and add the attachments to the deal record. If there's anything else you need for compliance review (evidence of redaction workflows, configuration playbook), Ben will provide the technical notes.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump on a short call with your compliance team if helpful.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
